question: Which of the following methods can be used to delete multiple columns simultaneously in Excel?

options.text: Select the columns, then right-click and press "Delete"
Select the columns, then press the Delete key
Use the "Clear" option from the Home tab

solution:
The correct answer is __Select the columns, then right-click and press **"Delete"**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Deleting multiple columns__ can be done easily in Excel.
 
• To delete multiple columns, first select the columns you want to remove by clicking and dragging across the column headers.
 
• Once selected, right-click on any of the highlighted column headers and choose "Delete" from the context menu.
 
• This method ensures that the selected columns are removed entirely, not just the data within them.
 
• Pressing the "Delete" key on the keyboard only clears the content of the cells without removing the columns.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Find and Replace:**
 
 
• The "Find and Replace" feature in Excel is used to locate specific text or values and replace them with new ones, not for deleting columns.
 
 
 
• **Clear Option:**
 
 
• The "Clear" option available in the Home tab only removes the contents, formatting, or comments from the cells, but does not delete the columns themselves.
 
 
 
• **Keyboard Delete Key:**
 
 
• Pressing the "Delete" key removes the data in the selected cells but does not delete the entire column.
